entries.name: Nothing matched at all
entries.when_to_use: The typed words and the photo tags match no entry.
entries.rule: Do not guess. Show this message and offer the two hand tests so the survivor can start.
entries.message: We could not match your words yet. Look at the ground: is there a white crust, standing water, or hard cracked clay? Crush a damp handful and drop a pinch in vinegar, then a pinch in baking soda, and tell us which one fizzes.

entries.name: A photo chip matched but no words
entries.when_to_use: A photo tag matches a chip but no typed word does.
entries.rule: Use the chip list in the photo cues file to point to the land conditions and gaps that chip stands for.
entries.message: We went by your picture. Here is the ground it looks like. If that is wrong, describe what you see in your own words.

entries.name: A land condition and a disease both matched
entries.when_to_use: The words match both a land condition and a disease.
entries.rule: Show the land condition first, then the disease it links to, because the ground is usually the cause.
entries.message: Your ground is the first thing to fix. Here is the land entry, then the crop problem it can cause.

entries.name: Several land conditions matched
entries.when_to_use: More than one land entry matches the same words or chips.
entries.rule: Count how many chips and words each entry matches. Show the entry with the most matches. If two are equal, ask one simple question.
entries.message: Tell us what the ground shows: a white crust, standing water, or hard dry cracks?

entries.name: Only a crop matched
entries.when_to_use: The words match a crop but no land condition.
entries.rule: Show the crop, then the land conditions and gaps it links to, so the ground is still explained.
entries.message: Here is the crop you asked about, together with the ground it suits. Check your ground first before you sow.

entries.name: Words about salt or a white crust
entries.when_to_use: Words such as salt, salty, white crust, white powder, salt patch.
entries.rule: Lead straight to the salty crust land entry, the salt gaps and the crust disease.
entries.message: This sounds like salty ground. Flush it with water and give it a way to drain before you sow anything.

entries.name: Words about too much water
entries.when_to_use: Words such as wet, soggy, swamp, waterlogged, standing water, root rot.
entries.rule: Lead to the waterlogged and flooded entries, the drainage gap and the yellowing disease.
entries.message: This sounds like water that cannot drain. Give it a way out before the roots drown.

entries.name: Words about dry hard cracked ground
entries.when_to_use: Words such as dry, cracked, dusty, drought, hard, baked, packed.
entries.rule: Lead to the dry and hard land entries, and the water and loosening gaps.
entries.message: This sounds like hard dry ground. Break the surface and get water into it before you sow.

entries.name: Words about dumping, spills or rubbish
entries.when_to_use: Words such as dump, spill, waste, chemical, oily, rusty, glass, barrel.
entries.rule: Lead straight to the debris or spill land entry and its safe water gap, with the keep away warning.
entries.message: Do not touch, grow or drink here. Keep people and animals away and ask a local elder or farmer to look at it first.

entries.name: Words and picture disagree
entries.when_to_use: The typed words point one way and the photo tag points another.
entries.rule: Trust the photo tag, because the picture shows the ground itself. Note the disagreement on screen.
entries.message: Your picture and your words disagree. We went with what the picture shows. If that is wrong, describe the ground again.

entries.name: Dangerous or unclear
entries.when_to_use: The words suggest harm to people or animals, or nothing is clear at all.
entries.rule: Show the safe warning and the local elder step. Never invent a cure or a fact.
entries.message: We are not sure this is safe. Nothing here replaces a local elder or farmer who can see the ground. Keep people and animals away until it is checked.

entries.name: Always show a trace
entries.when_to_use: Every time any answer is shown on screen.
entries.rule: Show the file path and the entry id under every answer, so each answer can be traced back to the exact entry.
entries.message: Every answer shows the file and the entry it came from, so you can always check where it came from. Ask a local elder or farmer for anything the entry leaves out.
